# The Dust That Becomes a Crown

## Scripture
"Look up at the sky and count the stars—if indeed you can count them... So shall your offspring be." — Genesis 15:5

## Reflection
Autumn evenings grow crisp and clear, and the sky seems to deepen, revealing stars that summer haze concealed. On such a night, long ago, God led Abraham outside his tent and made an impossible promise: descendants beyond counting, from a man with no heir and an aging wife.

Abraham had every reason to doubt. Yet Scripture tells us he "believed the Lord, and he credited it to him as righteousness" (Genesis 15:6). What changed? Not his circumstances—only his gaze. God didn't hand him a plan; He handed him a sky.

This is the quiet miracle of stargazing: it shifts our perspective without altering a single fact. The same problems remain when we lower our eyes. But we've seen something vast and faithful overhead, and we remember that the God who set each star in place has not forgotten the small tent where we dwell.

Perhaps you feel like Abraham tonight—waiting on a promise that seems written for someone else's life. Step outside. Let the cold air clear your thoughts. The One who calls each star by name also knows yours. In His economy, dust and promise are never far apart. The very ground you stand on was once stardust, and the God who formed galaxies from nothing specializes in making something from what looks like nothing at all.

## Prayer
Lord, when my circumstances seem small and my waiting feels long, lift my eyes to the heavens You made. Remind me that You are faithful to every promise, even when I cannot yet see its fulfillment. Grow my trust in the quiet, and let my gaze on Your vast creation renew my hope in Your nearness. Amen.
